title: The fibrewise unramified locus is open and base-change compatible
statement: Let $h:Z\to S$ be a locally finite type morphism [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Let $W_h$ be the union of all opens $O\subseteq Z$ on which $h|_O$ is unramified [def-weil-unramified-morphism]. Then $W_h$ is open and is precisely the set of $z\in Z$, $s=h(z)$, where the fibre $Z_s$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre] is unramified at $z$, meaning it has an unramified source neighbourhood in that fibre. Equivalently, $\mathcal O_{Z_s,z}=\kappa(z)$ via the residue map and $\kappa(z)/\kappa(s)$ is finite separable [def-weil-residue-field, def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension]. For any base change $h':Z'=Z\times_SS'\to S'$ with projection $g':Z'\to Z$ [def-pc-fibre-product], one has $W_{h'}=(g')^{-1}(W_h)$. No flatness or local finite presentation is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0475 (lemma-set-points-where-fibres-unramified), first assertion; the pointwise residue-field and fibre-local-ring characterization is Tag 02GF (lemma-unramified-at-point), (1), (2) and (6).

proof.text: Let T_h be the set of points z of Z for which h is unramified on some open neighbourhood of z. By the definition of W_h as the union of all such opens, W_h has underlying point set T_h. Stacks, Morphisms, Tag 0475 (lemma-set-points-where-fibres-unramified), identifies T_h with the set of points whose fibre Z_{h(z)} is unramified over the residue field at that point, proves that this set is open, and proves for every base change h' that T_{h'}=(g')^{-1}(T_h). For the forward inclusion in the base-change equality directly from the union description, base-change each unramified open using [lem-weil-pbc-unramified-base-change-open] (and its open-restriction clause); Tag 0475 supplies the converse and the pointwise identification. Therefore W_h is open, has the fibrewise description in the statement, and commutes with arbitrary base change.

Fix z in Z, put s=h(z), and write h_s:Z_s=Z×_S Spec κ(s)→Spec κ(s) for the fibre morphism. The fibre morphism is locally of finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-lft-base-change], applied to h and Spec κ(s)→S. Apply [lem-trf-unramified-maximal-ideal-residue-criterion] to h_s at z. Since the base local ring κ(s) is a field, its maximal ideal is zero; hence the criterion says that z is unramified in the fibre exactly when the maximal ideal of O_{Z_s,z} is zero and κ(z)/κ(s) is finite separable. The canonical residue map O_{Z_s,z}→κ(z) is then an isomorphism, and conversely that isomorphism says the maximal ideal is zero. This is precisely the displayed local-ring and residue-field characterization.

lean.statement: theorem unramifiedLocus_baseChange {Z S : Scheme.{u}} (h : Z ⟶ S) [LocallyOfFiniteType h] : IsOpen (unramifiedLocus h) ∧ (∀ z : Z, z ∈ unramifiedLocus h ↔ h.asFiber z ∈ unramifiedLocus (h.fiberToSpecResidueField (h z))) ∧ (∀ z : Z, z ∈ unramifiedLocus h ↔ IsIso ((h.fiber (h z)).residue (h.asFiber z)) ∧ (h.residueFieldMap z).hom.Finite ∧ @Algebra.IsSeparable (S.residueField (h z)) (Z.residueField z) _ _ (h.residueFieldMap z).hom.toAlgebra) ∧ (∀ {S' : Scheme.{u}} (k : S' ⟶ S), unramifiedLocus (pullback.snd h k) = (pullback.fst h k) ⁻¹' unramifiedLocus h)
